page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head centred at the top, page number top left. No margin notes. The right edge shows part of the facing page; it is not transcribed.

main_text.p: Immediata est, cum res alterans alterandae applicatur, nullo alio intercedente corpore medio.
Sic ignis circumfusum aerem immediatè alterat, aqua frigida manum, unguentum cutem vel carnem.
Mediata est,cum res alterans alterandam immutat alio intercedente corpore, per quod virtus alteratrix defertur.
Ita stellae alterant inferiorem hunc mundum, mediante aere interfuso, ignis aquam, mediante vase. Est hoc quod supra diximus, in omni motu requiri contactum seu vnionem moventis & mobilis.
main_text.head: II. In perfectivam & corruptivam.
main_text.p: Perfectiva est, quae qualitatem inducit, qua perficitur subiectum.

Sic virtutes & scientiae in animum inducuntur alteratione perfectiva. Virtutibus enim & scientiis perficitur animus: medicamenta salubria alterant aegrota corpora perficiendo ea, & ad pristinam integritatem reducendo, sive id fiat calefaciendo, sive frigefaciendo, sive humectando sive exsiccando.

page.notes: The right edge shows the facing page (a neighbouring page of the book with a running head and text in narrow columns), which is not transcribed. The Greek headings "Ἐξήγησις" are copied from a small, slightly blurred print; the first is marked [?] because its letters are less clear than the others. The heading "II. In perfectivam & corruptivam." is set apart on its own line and treated as a level 2 heading. The bare numbers XXXVII, XXXVIII, XXXIX and XL are written as paragraphs; XLI at the foot is a catchword.
